what_its_for: Bendamustine is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma called indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. It works by damaging the DNA inside cancer cells, which stops them from growing and spreading.
how_to_take: Bendamustine is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion, meaning it goes directly into your vein through a needle or catheter. A nurse or healthcare provider will give you this medicine at a clinic or hospital. You will NOT take this at home by mouth. Each infusion usually takes between 10 minutes and 1 hour depending on which brand and dose you receive. You will likely receive it on specific days of a treatment cycle, such as Day 1 and Day 2 of a 28-day cycle. Always tell your care team how you are feeling during and after the infusion.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your exact dose based on your body size (height and weight), the type of cancer being treated, and how well your kidneys and liver are working. A common dose range is 70 to 120 mg per square meter of body surface area. Do not try to adjust your dose on your own. Your dose may be lowered if you experience serious side effects. Your treatment team will monitor your blood counts regularly to make sure it is safe to continue.
missed_dose: Since bendamustine is given by a healthcare provider in a clinical setting, it is unlikely you will miss a dose on your own. However, if you are unable to make it to your scheduled appointment, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not try to make up a missed infusion on your own. Your doctor will decide the safest way to get you back on track with your treatment schedule.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home since it is prepared and given by healthcare professionals. The prepared infusion solution must be kept refrigerated and used within a specific time window depending on the brand. Your pharmacist or infusion team will handle all storage requirements according to the manufacturer guidelines.
what_to_avoid: Avoid being around people who are sick or have infections, as bendamustine lowers your immune system and makes it easier for you to get seriously ill. Avoid live vaccines (such as the flu nasal spray, shingles vaccine Zostavax, or MMR) during treatment unless your doctor approves. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they may interfere with how the drug works. Avoid alcohol during treatment as it can worsen side effects. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child during treatment, as bendamustine can seriously harm an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control during and for at least 6 months after treatment ends. Do not breastfeed while receiving this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following: fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, which may be a sign of infection; unusual bleeding or bruising; severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that you cannot control; shortness of breath or chest pain; rash, hives, or severe skin reactions; swelling of the face, lips, or throat; dark or cola-colored urine or yellowing of the skin or eyes which could signal liver problems; signs of a serious infusion reaction such as chills, itching, or feeling faint during the IV drip; or any new or worsening symptoms that worry you.
when_it_works: Bendamustine does not work overnight. Your doctor will monitor your response to treatment through blood tests and imaging scans. Some patients begin to see improvement within a few weeks to months of starting treatment. It is important to complete all scheduled treatment cycles even if you feel well, as stopping early may reduce how well the medicine works. Talk to your doctor about your specific treatment goals and what results to expect.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use bendamustine if you are pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while receiving this medicine. Kidney or liver problems: Your dose may need to be adjusted or the medicine may not be recommended if you have significant kidney or liver disease. Your doctor will check your organ function before and during treatment. Elderly patients (age 65 and older): Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Pediatric patients: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established.
